status_summary: EO 14171 (2025-01-20) reinstated the framework under the name Schedule Policy/Career. OPM published a final rule on 2026-02-06 (effective 2026-03-09) that keeps covered positions career but makes them at-will, outside chapter 75 adverse-action procedures and MSPB appeals. EO 14410 (2026-06-03) placed about 8,000 employees in more than 4,800 positions in the schedule, per press reports, against an earlier OPM estimate of up to 50,000. Lawsuits in D. Md. and D.D.C. are pending; the reports reviewed (through July 2026) describe no merits ruling and no injunction.

timeline.event: EO 14171 signed; it redesignates the 2020 Schedule F framework as Schedule Policy/Career. Agencies petition OPM and the President decides placement by later order, unlike the 2020 order under which OPM and agencies prepared position lists.
OPM publishes proposed rule 'Improving Performance, Accountability and Responsiveness in the Civil Service'. OPM later reported about 40,500 comments, roughly 94 percent opposed.

OPM final rule published in the Federal Register (effective 2026-03-09). It rescinds the 2024 OPM rule's limits and appeal rights and places covered employees outside chapter 75 and chapter 43 procedures.

In NTEU v. Trump (D.D.C.), the court accepts a schedule for NTEU to amend its complaint within 14 days of a presidential order placing positions in the schedule (per CRS). A parallel suit by PEER, AFGE and others is pending in D. Md.

EO 14410, Implementing Schedule Policy/Career in the Excepted Service, signed. An appendix lists the covered positions; agency heads have 7 days to notify employees. The order also directs separate bonus pools and OPM rulemaking on a Presidential award program.
OPM issues a memorandum and implementation materials for EO 14410.

Executive Order 14410, Implementing Schedule Policy/Career in the Excepted Service (signed 2026-06-03), is published at 91 FR 34893; it places the positions listed in its appendix in Schedule Policy/Career, amends Executive Order 13957 and the Civil Service Rules, adds a performance or misconduct removal basis, and gives agencies 7 days to notify affected employees.
Federal News Network reports close to 8,000 career employees notified of reclassification, three pending lawsuits, no court rulings reported, and no immediate plans for further designations.

Office of Government Ethics publishes an interim final rule (91 FR 46239, effective 2026-07-23, comments to 2026-08-24) keeping positions moved into Schedule Policy/Career at their prior financial disclosure filing status, so employees not previously required to file public reports remain exempt.

OPM proposes a rule, Employment in the Excepted Service (comments due 2026-11-17), updating excepted-service regulations to cover Schedule Policy/Career and Schedule G, including conversion of certain Pathways participants.

A federal-workforce litigation tracker updated this date lists three pending challenges to the June 2026 placement order (NTEU, AFGE, and Government Accountability Project with NARFE), with no merits ruling and no injunction reported.

title: Reinstate Schedule F for policy-influencing career positions
uncertainties: Latest litigation reports read run through early July 2026 and a tracker dated 2026-10-05. Searches on court rulings (2026-10-13) surfaced only March 2026 coverage and a CRS report; no ruling, injunction or removal under the schedule was found, but the dockets themselves were not opened. The 8,000 figure and 97 percent GS-15-or-above share come from press accounts of White House and OPM statements. One secondary source (FedSmith, 2026-06-03) says district court injunctions were stayed on appeal, which conflicts with Lawfare and Federal News Network reporting no rulings; it was not relied on. The Office of Government Ethics rule was read from its Federal Register API record (abstract only). An OPM direct final rule of 2026-08-14 cleaning up obsolete Civil Service Rules under EO 14410 section 2(g) was reviewed and left out of the timeline because it is non-substantive and does not touch the schedule.
